newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Arboyne revises Nonoc nickel resources.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Arboyne revises Nonoc nickel resources.

text.p: Nickel resources at the Nonoc nickel project in the Philippines has been revised, Arboyne NL said on Monday.

The revision puts measured and indicated resources for the project at 81.6 million tonnes, at a 0.9 percent nickel cut off, grading 1.16 percent nickel, 0.11 percent cobalt and 37.1 percent iron, Arboyne said.
Arboyne is seeking to rehabilitate the Nonoc complex, which includes a refinery capable of producing up to 65 million pounds of metal a year.

Arboyne said the revised estimation of laterite nickel resources available on Nonoc and South Dinagat Islands show nickel laterite mineralisation occurs as blanket-like deposits formed on ultramafic bedrock.
The laterites vary in thickness with topography but average seven metres on Nonoc and six metres on South Dinagat Island.
The profile comprises an upper limonite section (ferruginous zones 1 to 3 and a lower weathered serpentinite section zone 4).
Ore grade material occurs throughout the profile but peak nickel values are in zone four while peak cobalt values occur in zone three, it said.
The revised resource estimate was the result of a study by Vantage Mining Group, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Minproc Engineering Ltd.
Negotiations are well advanced to purchase higher grade limonite from other Philippine suppliers, the company said.
"This will allow a higher nickel feed grade to the refinery, it said.
Low metal prices and high energy costs coupled with a devalued Philippine peso and high interest rates forced operations to close in 1986.
Arboyne estimates it will cost about US$370 million to rehabilitate the operation.

Arboyne's entry to the project is through its option to acquire Pacific Holdings Ltd, a company that acquired Philinco Mining and Industrial Corp, which has concluded an agreement with the Philippines government for the purchase of Nonoc.
